why_threshold_crossed_now: A newly disclosed exploit drained about 8.7M FET (about $1.56M at incident value) from Fetch.ai's Ethereum TokenConversionManagerV3. SlowMist attributed the path to a valid single-EOA conversion-authorizer signature and reported that conversionIn lacked the on-chain burn/lock proof and amount-limit checks present on the opposite conversion path.

The same attacker cluster was linked by Blockaid/PeckShield reporting to roughly 408.5M unauthorized NTX originating from the NuNet deployer account, worth about $452K before/around the collapse; the attacker subsequently converted much of the proceeds into about 546.36 ETH.

This occurred immediately after FET had participated in a broader AI-token rotation. The security event therefore changes leadership quality inside an active narrative rather than merely affecting an isolated inactive token.

CoinGecko's current AI-category table still shows the broad AI category positive while Bittensor Subnets are outperforming it, indicating that speculative interest has not simply exited AI; it is becoming more selective after the FET/NTX security failure.

FET.name: Artificial Superintelligence Alliance / Fetch.ai
FET.reason: The incident demonstrates that an ecosystem-critical conversion path could be authorized through a compromised single EOA and did not independently verify a burn/lock proof or enforce the same amount-limit guard on conversionIn. This is a dangerous permission/authentication failure under the framework even though the exploit drained converter inventory rather than proving arbitrary mint authority over all FET supply.

NTX.name: NuNet
NTX.reason: Unauthorized token creation was linked to the deployer account itself; this directly fails privileged mint/deployer-control and suspicious-transfer gates. NTX subsequently fell more than 70% and printed a new all-time low in current reporting.

leadership_rotation.status: Bittensor/TAO retains relative AI leadership, but not a new paper-buy threshold
evidence: CoinGecko's current category table shows Bittensor Subnets outperforming the broader AI category on the day.
TAO rose from about $218.30 on Sep 15 to about $263.70 on Sep 19 while reported daily turnover rose from about $140.8M to $267.8M.

The dedicated Bittensor subnet category remains broad rather than TAO-only: Chutes, Lium, Targon, affine and Templar are all positive in the latest category snapshot, with Templar about +20% over seven days in that snapshot.
discounts: No fresh, independently funded cohort of historically selective TAO spot accumulators was verified in this run.
Bittensor remains materially emission-supported; the Sep 7 observation already classified TAO value capture as productive reserve/staking demand rather than a direct pro-rata cash claim.
Subnet token liquidity and holder-independence remain too thinly audited to surface a subnet token as a paper candidate merely because it is outperforming.

flow_quality.classification: sector-level discretionary AI rotation remains visible, but FET/NTX capital is now security-contaminated and cannot qualify
evidence: FET had rallied with the broader AI narrative before the exploit, so the subsequent drop is a security-driven relative-leadership break rather than proof that the whole AI theme ended.
Bittensor subnet breadth remains positive while the broad AI category is only modestly positive, supporting selective migration within the theme.
rejected_explanations: No new FET/NTX farming or points campaign is needed to explain the post-exploit divergence; the security incident itself is the dominant causal change.
Raw social mentions and influencer trade calls are not counted as confirmation.

wallet_quality.FET: not relevant enough to override the security failure; reported pre-exploit exchange withdrawals are explicitly discounted
wallet_quality.TAO: NO_UPGRADE: no fresh verified selective-wallet convergence
wallet_quality.NTX: FAIL: attacker/deployer-linked mint dominates all ordinary holder-flow evidence

liquidity_and_executability.FET: Globally liquid enough to sell, but structural/security gate blocks a new paper entry.
liquidity_and_executability.TAO: Globally executable, but no new confirmation tranche is justified.
liquidity_and_executability.NTX: Rejected regardless of nominal liquidity because unauthorized supply creation/deployer control fails the hard gate.

portfolio_impact.notes: The paper portfolio has no FET, NTX or TAO position. Existing holdings remain subject to their prior regime tests; this AI-sector event does not justify reallocating from them without a qualifying positive candidate.

forward_tests: For FET: require an official technical postmortem, rotation/revocation of compromised authorization, proof that the vulnerable converter path is disabled or repaired, and independent confirmation that no additional privileged path can release inventory without an on-chain burn/lock proof.

For NTX: require proof that deployer/mint authority has been remediated, unauthorized supply treatment is resolved, and holder/liquidity structure is reconstructed; until then the token remains structurally rejected.
For TAO: require fresh independent selective-wallet accumulation plus continued subnet breadth and customer-funded economic activity before a paper starter is reconsidered.
